title: 100 Things to Talk About With Your Crush
h1: 100 Things to Talk About With Your Crush (So You Never Run Out)
description: Never run out of things to talk about with your crush. Here are 100 easy conversation topics and questions for texting, hanging out and getting closer.
keyword: things to talk about with your crush
excerpt: 100 easy, fun things to talk about with your crush, from light icebreakers to personal stories and flirty questions, plus tips for keeping it natural.
intro:
Talking to your crush should be the fun part. So why does your mind go completely blank the second they say hi? It happens to almost everyone. When you really like someone, you want every conversation to go well, and that pressure makes it harder to think of anything to say.

This list of 100 things to talk about with your crush is here to help. The topics are grouped from easy and lighthearted to more personal and a little flirty, so you can pick the right level for where you are. Use them in person or over text, and don't worry about getting through them all. One good topic is often all it takes to get the conversation flowing.
body:
How to use these conversation topics

  • Start light. Easy topics like food, music and weekend plans help you both relax before getting more personal.
  • Follow their energy. If your crush lights up talking about a hobby, stay there. The best conversations go wherever the enthusiasm is.
  • Share as much as you ask. Answer your own questions so it feels like a back-and-forth, not an interview.
  • Listen for hooks. Small details they mention, like a trip, a sibling or a pet, make great follow-up topics later.
  • Keep it comfortable. Save heavier topics until you know each other better, and let them skip anything they don't want to answer.
Tip: Pick three topics from this list before you see your crush or open the chat. Having a few ideas ready takes the panic out of awkward pauses.

Easy icebreakers to get things going

  1. What's the best thing that happened to you this week?
  2. Any fun plans for the weekend?
  3. What are you watching right now?
  4. Coffee, tea or neither?
  5. What's the last song you had on repeat?
  6. Which local restaurant is seriously underrated?
  7. Are you a morning person or a night owl?
  8. What's the weirdest food combination you secretly love?
  9. Beach vacation or mountain cabin?
  10. Have you read or watched anything lately that you couldn't stop thinking about?
  11. What's your go-to comfort snack?
  12. Do you have a favorite holiday? Why that one?
  13. What app do you spend way too much time on?
  14. What's the best concert or live event you've been to?
  15. Cats, dogs or something more unusual?

Fun hypotheticals and "would you rather" topics

  1. If you could live anywhere in the world for a year, where would you go?
  2. Would you rather be able to talk to animals or speak every language?
  3. If you won the lottery tomorrow, what's the first thing you'd buy?
  4. What superpower would you pick, and what would you actually use it for?
  5. If you could have dinner with anyone, living or not, who would it be?
  6. Would you rather time travel to the past or the future?
  7. If your life were a movie, what genre would it be?
  8. What would your perfect day look like if money and time didn't matter?
  9. If you could instantly become an expert at something, what would you choose?
  10. Would you rather never use social media again or never watch TV again?
  11. If you were famous, what would you be famous for?
  12. What fictional world would you most want to live in?
  13. Would you rather have a rewind button or a pause button for your life?
  14. If you could only eat one cuisine forever, which would it be?
  15. What's one thing you'd do if you knew you couldn't fail?

Personal life topics to get to know them

  1. Where did you grow up, and what was it like?
  2. Do you have siblings? What are they like?
  3. What did you want to be when you were a kid?
  4. What's a family tradition you love?
  5. What's your favorite memory from childhood?
  6. Who's your best friend, and how did you meet?
  7. What's something you're really proud of?
  8. What's the best trip you've ever taken?
  9. What do you do when you need to relax?
  10. What's something about you that surprises people?
  11. What's the best advice anyone has ever given you?
  12. What's a skill you'd love to learn?
  13. What does your ideal weekend look like?
  14. What are you most looking forward to this year?
  15. Who's someone you really look up to?

Hobbies, passions and interests

  1. What's something you could talk about for hours?
  2. How did you get into your favorite hobby?
  3. What's a hobby you tried and quit?
  4. Do you play any sports or have a team you follow?
  5. What's the best book you've ever read?
  6. What show could you rewatch forever?
  7. Do you play video games? Which ones?
  8. Are you into cooking? What's your best dish?
  9. What kind of music do you listen to when no one's around?
  10. Are you more of an outdoors person or a cozy-indoors person?
  11. What's a creative thing you enjoy, like drawing, writing or making music?
  12. What podcast or YouTube channel do you recommend to everyone?
  13. What's something new you've been curious to try?
  14. Is there a cause or issue you really care about?
  15. What's your dream concert lineup?

Deeper topics for when you're closer

  1. What's something you've changed your mind about recently?
  2. What makes you feel most like yourself?
  3. What's a fear you've gotten over?
  4. What do you value most in a friendship?
  5. What's the hardest thing you've ever done?
  6. Where do you see yourself in five years?
  7. What's a lesson you learned the hard way?
  8. What's something people often get wrong about you?
  9. What does a meaningful life look like to you?
  10. What's a goal you haven't told many people about?
  11. When do you feel the happiest?
  12. Do you think people can really change?
  13. What's something you wish you were better at?
  14. What's a moment that changed how you see the world?
  15. What do you think makes a relationship work?

Lightly flirty topics

  1. What's your idea of a perfect date?
  2. What's the first thing you notice about someone?
  3. Do you believe in love at first sight?
  4. What's the most romantic thing someone has done for you?
  5. What's your love language?
  6. What's a cheesy movie you secretly love?
  7. What makes someone instantly more attractive to you?
  8. What was your first impression of me? Be honest.
  9. What's the best compliment you've ever gotten?
  10. Are you more of a planner or spontaneous when it comes to dates?
  11. What's your favorite thing to do on a rainy day with someone?
  12. What song would you pick for a slow dance?
  13. Do you think opposites attract, or do similar people work better?
  14. What's a small gesture that would totally win you over?
  15. If we went on an adventure together, where should we go?

Topics for texting your crush

  1. Send a photo of something funny you saw and ask what they think.
  2. Ask for a recommendation: a show, a song or a place to eat.
  3. Follow up on something they mentioned, like a test, game or interview.
  4. Share a meme that reminds you of an inside joke.
  5. Ask them to settle a silly debate, like whether a hot dog is a sandwich.
  6. Tell them about something good that happened in your day.
  7. Ask what they're up to tonight and suggest joining if it feels right.
  8. Send a song and say it made you think of them.
  9. Ask a rapid-fire "this or that" question.
  10. Wish them luck before something important.

Topics to avoid early on

Some subjects can feel heavy or awkward before you know each other well. It's usually best to wait on:

  • Detailed stories about your exes or why past relationships ended
  • Gossip or criticism about mutual friends
  • Hot-button debates, unless you know you both enjoy them
  • Very personal questions about money, health or family conflict
  • Pressuring them to define what you are

None of these are off-limits forever. They're just easier to discuss once trust has grown.

Keep the conversation going

The secret to great conversations isn't a perfect list of topics. It's curiosity. Ask follow-up questions like "How did that happen?" or "What was that like?" and share your own stories in return. If there's a pause, that's okay; a smile and a new topic usually fixes it. For more help, read how to keep a conversation going, try our deep questions to ask your boyfriend once things get serious, or look for the signs your crush likes you. If you're starting over text, our guide on how to start a conversation with a guy over text has easy openers.
takeaways: Start with light topics and move toward personal ones as you get comfortable.
Follow your crush's enthusiasm and ask natural follow-up questions.
Share your own answers so the conversation feels balanced.
Save heavy topics like exes and money for when you know each other better.

faq.q: What should I talk about with my crush?
faq.a: Start with easy topics like music, shows, food, weekend plans and hobbies. As you get comfortable, move to personal topics like childhood memories, goals and things they care about. Fun hypotheticals and light flirty questions work well too. Follow whatever topic makes them light up.

faq.q: How do I not run out of things to say to my crush?
faq.a: Ask open-ended questions and follow up on their answers instead of jumping to new topics. Share your own stories in return. Remember details they mentioned earlier and bring them back up. Having a few topics in mind beforehand also helps when there's a pause.

faq.q: What do you text your crush to start a conversation?
faq.a: Try something easy to answer and specific: ask for a recommendation, follow up on something they mentioned, send a funny meme or ask a quick this-or-that question. Avoid a plain "hey" on its own, since it doesn't give them much to respond to.

faq.q: How can I tell if my crush enjoys talking to me?
faq.a: Good signs include asking you questions back, giving detailed answers, keeping the conversation going, texting you first sometimes and remembering things you've said. If they seem engaged and happy to talk, that's encouraging. Short replies every time may mean they're busy or less interested.
